newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK market tops in derivative warrant trading - SFC.
newsitem.headline: HK market tops in derivative warrant trading - SFC.

text.p: More derivative warrants are listed and trading on the Hong Kong stock market than any other exchange in the world, the head of the territory's securities watchdog said.

"At the end of last year, we had 296 listed derivative warrants, which makes us in fact the largest listed and traded derivative warrants market in the world," Securities and Futures Commission chairman Anthony Neoh said on Tuesday.
These were very actively traded on the Hong Kong stock exchange, he said.
"Luxembourg actually has more listed warrants, but dealing is not on the exchange," said Neoh.
The territory's chief securities' regulator saw his role chiefly as a facilitator of trade not a controller, he told an American Chamber of Commerce meeting in Hong Kong.
"I regard regulation as not just enforcing the rules. I regard regulation as a process of creation of the right conditions for markets to thrive," Neoh said.
As at end 1996, there were more than 1,300 listed securities in Hong Kong, including 601 listed companies, Neoh said.
Market capitalisation of the Hong Kong market exceeded US$400 billion, Neoh added.
At the market's record close of 14,236.20 on Tuesday, market capitalisation was estimated to have risen to US$499 billion.
The futures market was also very active with more than 4.5 million futures contracts traded in 1996, he said.

"The interesting thing is that the options market has grown quite phenomenally, in particular the Hang Seng Index options market, which makes the Hong Kong a very sophisticated derivatives market," Neoh said.
This was partly due to the rise in the number of overseas controlled dealers active in the Hong Kong market, and the heavy participation of institutional investors, he said.
"Our market is tending toward a very high segmentation on the institutional side of things," the chairman said. "We find that our market now is between 56 percent and 60 percent institutional."
Neoh said Hong Kong was the largest institutional market in Asia outside of Japan.
There were more than 1,300 funds authorised in Hong Kong, the largest of any jurisdiction in Asia, which were managed by about 100 investment management firms, he said.
